::: {#sol-euler-polynomial}

1. The values are $41$, $43$, $47$ and $53$, which are all prime.
2. Take $n = 41$:
   $41^2 + 41 + 41 = 41 \cdot (41 + 1 + 1) = 41 \cdot 43$,
   which is not prime.
   The value $n = 40$ also fails:
   $40^2 + 40 + 41 = 1681 = 41^2$.

The claim held for every value we checked in part 1,
and it is still false:
checking some cases cannot prove a universal claim.

:::
